title: Ergodic nonlocal Jacobi semigroups with positive invariant densities for nonzero finite downward-jump kernels
source_title: On non-local ergodic Jacobi semigroups: spectral theory, convergence-to-equilibrium and contractivity
author: Patrick Cheridito; Pierre Patie; Anna Srapionyan; Aditya Vaidyanathan
difficulty_reason: The classical Jacobi semigroup and Bernstein-function prerequisites do not themselves construct the nonlocal generator with the stated positive invariant density. The author proves the necessary moment factorisation and full support, builds an explicit polynomial intertwining and maximum-principle/resolvent argument, and transfers the invariant measure without assuming the resulting Markov process exists. Those constructions then establish the polynomial core, invariant-law uniqueness and ergodicity in the genuinely nonzero jump-kernel case.

proof_review.note: Full article retained as conservative closed context for notation, global assumptions, diagrams and references. Exact primary and supporting physical proof pages are recorded separately. Theorem2.1 restricted to genuinely nonzero h satisfying all of AssumptionA: nonnegative integrable h on(1,infinity), finite positive Radon jump measure Pi=−(e^r h(e^r))prime dr, mu>integral h, and lambda1>mu+indicator(mu<1+integral h). Full moment determinacy, density support/positivity and Markov-generator construction read. Classical h=0 branch excluded so no copied transformed-parameter inequalities from that branch needed. New elementary intertwining, maximum principle, resolvent polynomial recursion and invariant-measure uniqueness are provided explicitly; prior multiplicative-kernel/Bernstein-gamma facts are named research prerequisites. The Hille–Yosida–Ray theorem and classical beta Jacobi boundary/core facts are explicit standard foundations. No spectral expansion, contractivity or entropy-rate claim selected. Printed27 claim both roots of n²+(lambda1−1)n+q are negative is not needed: the explicit recurrence only uses positive denominators for integer n≥0,q>0,lambda1>1.

historical_source_pdf_evidence.original_difficulty_reason: Bernstein-function Wiener–Hopf factorization, multiplicative moment kernels and an intertwining-based Feller construction produce a non-self-adjoint jump semigroup and its unique positive invariant law.
